Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (in no particular order). These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have been praised for their storytelling, performances, and atmospheric tension.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that blends horror elements with a sharp critique of domestic abuse. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman who suspects her abusive ex‑partner has found a way to become literally invisible. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced, witty style shines in this gangster caper about a British drug lord trying to sell his empire. The film balances humor with tense plot twists. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | Though more courtroom drama than pure crime‑thriller, its exploration of political intrigue and civil disobedience makes it a compelling watch. Sorkin’s razor‑sharp dialogue keeps viewers on edge. |
| 4 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling epic that uses de-aging tech to follow mob life over decades. Scorsese’s masterful direction and the stellar cast make it a must‑see for fans of crime sagas. |
| 5 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh & Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | Sandler’s manic portrayal of a charismatic jeweler spiraling into debt is both unsettling and oddly endearing. The film’s frenetic pacing mirrors the protagonist’s chaotic life. |
| 6 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A visceral revenge story set in 19th‑century Tasmania. While not a conventional crime‑thriller, its brutal depiction of colonial violence and the quest for justice resonates strongly. |
| 7 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish thriller that follows a man falsely accused of child abuse. The film’s tense atmosphere and moral ambiguity make it a standout in the genre. |
| 8 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime‑thriller that examines truth, honor, and gender dynamics in medieval France. Scott’s meticulous production design and strong ensemble cast elevate the narrative. |
| 9 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish dystopian thriller that uses a vertical prison setting to explore class conflict and human nature. Its allegorical approach adds depth to the crime‑thriller framework. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** (2019‑2020 release) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that blends horror elements with a sharp critique of domestic abuse. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman who suspects her abusive ex‑partner has found a way to become literally invisible. |

### How to Watch

- **Streaming**: Many of these titles are available on major platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, and HBO Max. Check your local listings or use a streaming aggregator like JustWatch to find where each film is currently hosted.
- **Physical Media**: If you prefer Blu‑ray or DVD, retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart carry most of these releases. Some titles may also be available through specialty stores like FandangoNow or Redbox.

Enjoy diving into these gripping crime‑thrillers!
